experiments.title: Diagnostic completion
experiments.hypothesis: Two legal-observation native OpenBW clients can complete a headless game and emit replay files.
experiments.conclusion: Supported for WorkerRush versus Idle; competitive strength and long-match synchronization remain unverified.

experiments.title: Competitive bot ports
experiments.hypothesis: McRave and ZZZKBot can run natively without disabling gameplay.
experiments.notes: Both native ports completed real headless games and passed official BWAPI header compilation. The cohort remains uncalibrated and source revisions are not ladder binary matches.
experiments.conclusion: McRave and ZZZKBot are runnable native ports with archived replays; broader reliability and strength calibration remain separate.

experiments.title: Scenario control and repeatability
experiments.hypothesis: Matched map, seed, revision, and launch settings will make repeated games suitable for calibration.
experiments.notes: Fixture runs exercised the 424242 scenario-control path; these are calibration infrastructure checks, not strength evidence.
experiments.conclusion: Three controlled fixture runs completed or recorded with stable scenario inputs; calibration still requires representative bot games.

experiments.title: UAlbertaBot cross-race port
experiments.hypothesis: The MIT UAlbertaBot port can complete a native OpenBW cross-race game with normal gameplay systems enabled.
experiments.notes: Protoss UAlbertaBot versus Zerg ZZZKBot completed on Benzene; this is compatibility evidence, not historical ladder strength evidence.
experiments.conclusion: Completed with verified opposing results, LF3, zero exits, and archived replays.

experiments.title: McRave defeat shutdown repair
experiments.hypothesis: The McRave lifecycle repair will eliminate the post-defeat Destination crash without changing strategic behavior.
experiments.notes: AddressSanitizer verification was clean, but its result metadata had an opposing-winner failure caveat; release verification later completed with opposing results, LF3, empty stderr, and two hashed replays.
experiments.conclusion: Lifecycle reliability evidence improved; the ASAN caveat means this does not establish full reliability or strategic equivalence.

experiments.title: OpenBW shutdown and timer lifetime repairs
experiments.hypothesis: Correcting queued-handler and timer state lifetimes will eliminate the reproduced engine memory errors without changing bot policies.
experiments.notes: Exact Destination seed-1002 release reproduction and full default AddressSanitizer check completed. Earlier partial shared-state builds were superseded after review caught two pointer-value predicates; they remain archived.
experiments.conclusion: Verified opposing terminal results, zero exits, empty stderr and two replays in both corrected checks. This establishes the tested lifetime paths, not broad synchronization correctness.

experiments.title: Profile the slow McRave cross-race game
experiments.hypothesis: McRave policy work dominates the slow Destination game; a source subsystem will account for at least 20% of sampled runtime.
experiments.notes: Ten seconds of sampling yielded 7,780 main-thread samples. Both clients completed the profiled game; instrumentation and different openings limit performance comparison.
experiments.conclusion: Goal assignment accounted for 47.6% of samples, with repeated ground-distance calculations at 45.8%. Repeated nearest-unit scans recompute paths for a growing army. No policy change was made in this experiment.

experiments.title: Cache distances within goal assignment
experiments.hypothesis: Reusing ground distances within one assignment call will reduce repeated path searches while preserving selection order.
experiments.notes: Official-header compilation and an ordered model check passed. Candidate and baseline selected different randomized openings; comparison engines also differed. No complete candidate replay was emitted before the wall cap.
experiments.conclusion: Candidate reached 231.8 frames/s versus 189.9 in a prior unsampled run, but both timed out and trajectories differed. This is preliminary performance evidence; no causal speedup, strength gain or baseline adoption is established. A controlled bot-seed comparison is next.

experiments.title: Compare goal caching with seeded openings
experiments.hypothesis: With matching engine and bot seeds, the distance cache improves throughput while preserving compatible early commands.
experiments.notes: Four games completed cleanly, and the openings matched within both pairs. The command-compatibility gate failed at frame 3: worker order and tied mineral targets differed. Source inspection traced this to containers ordered by object pointers.
experiments.conclusion: Candidate throughput was 7.78% and 10.99% higher, but differing trajectories prevent a causal performance claim. No strength gain or baseline promotion. A subsequent stable-traversal repeat also failed; compare both selectors on identical live states next.

experiments.title: Check whether unit-ID traversal repeats
experiments.hypothesis: Sorting workers and minerals by public unit ID will make identical seeded opening commands repeatable.
experiments.notes: Two identical baseline games completed, but raw commands differed at frame 2 and mineral targets differed at frame 3. Source inspection found that OpenBW BWAPI assigns public unit IDs in first-access order from a pointer-hashed container.
experiments.conclusion: The repeatability gate failed. No candidate game was launched and no speed or strength comparison was made. Further traversal changes were stopped as planned.

experiments.title: Correct station defense coordinates
experiments.hypothesis: One station-defense insertion stores a relative offset where consumers require an absolute map tile; correcting it will remove invalid defense candidates.
experiments.notes: The diagnostic baseline exposed out-of-map defense (0,-3) at base (64,118). The one-line candidate produced absolute tile (64,115), and all recorded defense entries were valid. Both games completed and retained both-player replays.
experiments.conclusion: The replay confirms an accepted Creep Colony build at corrected tile (64,115), frame 3,542. Accept the coordinate repair for integration; no win-rate or strength improvement is inferred from these two games.

experiments.title: Compare goal selectors on identical live states
experiments.hypothesis: The cached and original goal selectors choose identical ordered units from the same live state, while caching reduces distance queries.
experiments.notes: The corrected diagnostic completed 5,780 goal-assignment calls and 2,124 actual selections with zero differences between both shadow selectors and original gameplay. A pre-review attempt was interrupted and preserved.
experiments.conclusion: The largest call had three eligible units and requested two. The required large-state coverage was 20 eligible and 10 requested, so this does not validate the profiled hotspot or establish a speed improvement.

experiments.title: Exercise goal caching with the profiled opening
experiments.hypothesis: Reusing the opening from the profiled slow game will expose large real goal-selection calls and allow both algorithms to be compared on identical states.
experiments.notes: The targeted diagnostic compared 53,828 real calls and 352,160 actual selections with zero divergences. First qualifying state: 48 eligible units, 10 requested; largest recorded state: 154 eligible, 22 requested. It hit its 180-second instrumentation cap and emitted no final result or replay.
experiments.conclusion: The registered large-state equivalence gate passed. Cached selection made 1,243,302 distance calls versus 15,122,188 original calls (91.78% fewer). Accept this evidence for a release-build quick check; these timings and the partial game establish no production speed or strength gain.

experiments.title: McRave coordinate repair and goal-cache quick check
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen coordinate-repair and invocation-cache build completes the ten-game suite cleanly and sustains at least 384 durable frames per second.
experiments.notes: Nine verified games: eight wins and one loss. All 20 replays retained. The final game had two winner=true callbacks despite zero exits, and remains unscored. Overall 403.0 fps; five games below 384, slowest 322.5. Failure subtype corrected with raw collection preserved.
experiments.conclusion: The registered reliability and per-match performance requirements failed. Resolve the outcome conflict and profile the remaining slow cases before adoption. Results are uncalibrated and do not establish a causal strength improvement.

experiments.title: Stardust native compatibility smoke
experiments.hypothesis: The pinned Stardust source can run its normal Protoss gameplay path as a native ARM64 module against this project's OpenBW ABI.
experiments.notes: Frozen package b6097c9a5d972afc4d687ed51f0d001af36f50a93dc625d66eb546bd02f6080c ran against WorkerRush Zerg on Benzene with engine seed 5201 and a 120-second limit. Both processes exited zero, results opposed, LF3 held, stderr was empty, and both replays were retained.
experiments.conclusion: Native ABI interoperability and one complete smoke game are established. This single match does not estimate strength, timing representativeness, broader matchup/map compatibility, or tournament eligibility.
experiments.limitations: Uncalibrated; one game; Stardust wall-clock and address-dependent behavior uncontrolled; derivative competition use requires written author permission.

experiments.title: Profile McRave after goal caching
experiments.hypothesis: A remaining cohesive subsystem accounts for at least 20% of main-thread samples after goal caching.
experiments.notes: One preregistered 10-second sample after frame 10,080: 7,843 main-thread samples. BWEB path generation appears in at least 22.08%; goal-distance work in 0.24%; visual work in at most 0.13%. The game completed with opposing results.
experiments.conclusion: Investigate flying-navigation path generation. This sampled interval identifies CPU work; it does not establish a speedup or playing-strength improvement.

experiments.title: Investigate conflicting engine winners
experiments.hypothesis: One attempt with the failing scenario inputs may reproduce reciprocal winner callbacks and identify the terminal event ordering.
experiments.notes: The original game has contradictory local replays with reciprocal Dropped events. The one registered reproduction completed with opposing results on a different trajectory. Source review shows several engine paths produce the same drop code.
experiments.conclusion: The cause is unresolved. Preserve the original as unscored and identify the drop source with an isolated diagnostic build before changing engine behavior.

experiments.title: Identify engine drop causes
experiments.hypothesis: Logging the first engine drop source and terminal callback ordering will distinguish routine cleanup from the historical conflicting-winner failure.
experiments.notes: One WorkerRush/Idle control and one competitive attempt both completed normally. Both showed defeat, then victory 31 frames later. Their first drop followed an action from an already-defeated player; neither logged a state-hash mismatch.
experiments.conclusion: The original failure remains unclassified. Retain diagnostic logging for subsequent experiments; no shutdown-protocol change is justified by these runs.

experiments.title: Compare A* bounds checks on identical inputs
experiments.hypothesis: Caching map dimensions within each A* search preserves reachability, distance, ordered path tiles and callback counts.
experiments.notes: One registered game compared 13,439 calls, including 8,509 valid flying searches, 4,928 valid ground searches and two invalid-endpoint probes. There were zero mismatches. Independent source review passed. No naturally failed valid search occurred.
experiments.conclusion: Build a production candidate for a separate throughput evaluation. The shadow check establishes equivalence for observed calls, not a speed or strength improvement.

experiments.title: Stardust cross-race compatibility check
experiments.hypothesis: The native Stardust port completes four cross-race games with plausible production and at least 384 durable frames per second in each game.
experiments.notes: Three wins from three clean games, all above 1,700 fps. The first game crashed in Stardust mining optimization; it remains a failure. Replay commands show Protoss worker, building and combat production in every game. No state-hash mismatch was logged.
experiments.conclusion: Repair the mining-optimizer crash before accepting Stardust as a reliable opponent. These four games do not establish local Elo or BASIL-equivalent strength.

experiments.title: McRave A* bounds throughput check
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen A* dimension-snapshot candidate completes ten fixed games cleanly with at least 384 durable logical frames per wall second in every game and in aggregate.
experiments.notes: Ten wins from ten clean games, with opposing results, no state-hash mismatch and 20 archived replays. Games 5–10 missed the 384 fps floor; aggregate throughput was 373.9 fps. The fixed cohort is uncalibrated and does not establish a strength improvement.
experiments.conclusion: The registered performance gate failed. Preserve this candidate as an experiment and investigate repeated pathfinding callback work before another throughput check.

experiments.title: Diagnose Stardust mining timer exhaustion
experiments.hypothesis: Excluding the only remaining timer value leaves an empty prediction set that the mining forecast cannot safely consume.
experiments.notes: One preregistered probe stopped deliberately at frame 765 after observing the set change from {0} to empty. The original crash and this diagnostic attempt remain archived.
experiments.conclusion: The empty prediction set is confirmed. Test a conservative fallback in a separate fork; this deliberate abort provides no strength result.

experiments.title: Repair Stardust mining timer exhaustion
experiments.hypothesis: Restoring the possible nonzero timer values after a contradictory prediction prevents the confirmed empty-set failure while keeping the mining optimizer active.
experiments.notes: The single registered probe completed with opposing results, no state-hash mismatch and replay evidence of worker, building and combat production. Recovery occurred at least eight times; the defensive forecast fallback was not used.
experiments.conclusion: The focused repair probe passed. Evaluate the frozen fork in the four-game compatibility cohort before accepting it as an opponent.

experiments.title: Validate the repaired Stardust fork
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen mining-timer repair completes all four cross-race scenarios cleanly with plausible gameplay and at least 384 durable fps in every game and in aggregate.
experiments.notes: Four wins from four clean games. Every game exceeded 1,999 fps; aggregate throughput was 2,059.4 fps. No state-hash mismatch or defensive forecast fallback occurred. Replay commands show worker, building and combat production in every game.
experiments.conclusion: Accept this frozen fork as a provisional local opponent. The original port remains rejected; this compatibility check does not establish a local Elo or transfer the upstream BASIL rating.

experiments.title: Compare cached pathfinding queries on identical inputs
experiments.hypothesis: Caching heuristic and walkability results within one search preserves each path while reducing repeated queries.
experiments.notes: The one registered game completed normally. All 13,611 valid searches and two invalid-endpoint probes matched reachability, distance bits and ordered tiles; combined callback evaluations fell 91.02%. There was no state-hash mismatch.
experiments.conclusion: The observed equivalence check passed. Build a separate production candidate and measure it against the unchanged throughput gate; this diagnostic ran both algorithms and does not measure production speed.

experiments.title: McRave pathfinding memoization throughput check
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen per-search A* memoization candidate completes ten fixed games cleanly with at least 384 durable logical frames per wall second in every game and in aggregate.
experiments.notes: Ten clean wins, with opposing results, no state-hash mismatch and 20 hash-checked, parsed replays. Aggregate throughput reached 413.1 fps, but games 6–9 fell below 384; the slowest ran at 269.5 fps.
experiments.conclusion: The registered per-game performance gate failed. Preserve this candidate and profile the slowest scenario later in the game before choosing another optimization. These reused scenarios do not establish a causal speedup or strength improvement.

experiments.title: Profile McRave late in the game
experiments.hypothesis: A complete ten-second sample after frame 15,000 identifies a cohesive subsystem occupying at least 20% of main-thread observations.
experiments.notes: The match completed normally. The sample retained 7,165 stacks: Combat 23.8%, grid updates 18.9%, Support 11.8%. Its timestamp precedes game completion by only 9.110 seconds, so the required ten seconds of live sampling could not be established.
experiments.conclusion: Keep these counts as partial diagnostic evidence. Investigate repeated ground-path and Support path generation with a separately registered diagnostic; this sample does not pass its original gate.

experiments.title: Calibrate a local league on two new maps
experiments.hypothesis: Five exact build/race configurations complete twelve clean comparisons and form a connected graph on two previously unused maps.
experiments.notes: All twelve attempted; nine clean and three conflicting-winner outcomes. All24 replays parse and match owner frames. Local estimates retain broad model-dependent intervals and prior sensitivity.
experiments.conclusion: The clean-cohort gate failed. Show the nine reviewed games as a partial uncalibrated league; investigate McRave–Stardust terminal integrity and McRave losses on Heartbreak Ridge. No promotion or BASIL estimate.

experiments.notes: Part of the preregistered twelve-game local-calibration-v1 cohort. See the parent evaluation for the decision and uncertainty.
experiments.conclusion: Included only after per-game review; failures remain unscored. This sub-batch alone does not promote a bot.

experiments.title: First native game for Kestrel, our original bot
experiments.hypothesis: Kestrel completes a real headless match and demonstrates economy, production, scouting and combat.
experiments.notes: Both processes exited cleanly and both replays parsed. Kestrel lost to WorkerRush; repeated building commands and no trained combat unit failed the lifecycle gate.
experiments.conclusion: Keep the first replay and fix pending construction management before further strength evaluation. A diagnostic-fixture loss is not a calibrated rating.

experiments.title: Kestrel completes its production and combat lifecycle
experiments.hypothesis: Preserving the pending builder allows the original lifecycle to complete with at most 12 pylon/gateway build commands.
experiments.notes: Kestrel won its WorkerRush diagnostic smoke. Replay and telemetry show 27 probes,5 pylons,4 gateways,9 zealots and 2 dragoons at peak; both replays parse and terminal results agree.
experiments.conclusion: The lifecycle passed, but 16 build commands exceed the registered 12-command ceiling. Retain as the first working lifecycle reference; continue command management. This fixture is not a rating anchor.

experiments.title: Kestrel faces ZZZK and UAlberta
experiments.hypothesis: The original bot completes two benchmark games with plausible production, fewer rejected commands and at least 384 durablefps.
experiments.notes: Both games completed with opposing outcomes and parsed replays; Kestrel lost both. ZZZK:2557fps and 18% commands rejected. UAlberta:3287fps and 71% rejected;16 pylon/gateway orders.
experiments.conclusion: Compatibility and lifecycle passed, but the command-quality gate failed. Fix repeated attack requests before expanding the strength cohort. Two losses do not provide a calibrated Elo.

experiments.title: Measure repeated McRave path searches
experiments.hypothesis: A bounded real-game diagnostic identifies a directly observed regeneration case representing at least 20% and 100 generated paths for a semantics-preserving shadow comparison.
experiments.notes: Support generated 24,676 JPS results;23,795 were unreachable. Combat march generated 36,180 and retreat 33,569. Match ended cleanly with two retained replays.
experiments.conclusion: Adopt the next diagnostic step only: test fresh per-search JPS callback memoization and count cheap rejection separately. No caching across frames, speed claim or bot promotion.
